problem: The wording is misleading. It says subtracting the drop 'after division gives the wrong answer', but algebraically (Vm − Vd)/π = Vm/π − Vd/π, so subtracting Vd/π after the division is exactly right. A student can read this and think any post-division subtraction is forbidden.
fix: Reword: 'Subtract Vd from the peak first: Vdc = (Vm − Vd)/π. Do not subtract the full 0.7 V from the already-divided value; only 0.7/π = 0.22 V may come off after the division.'

problem: 'The DC output doubles' is unqualified. It is true only when the peak per half-winding Vm is the same as the half-wave peak. With one 12-0-12 transformer, using the whole 24 V winding in a half-wave circuit gives the same Vdc as the centre-tap connection.
fix: 'The DC output doubles for the same peak Vm, because two humps per cycle replace one.'

problem: Silicon Schottky diodes have low reverse-voltage ratings, so they are not used in the bridge that sits directly on a 230 V mains (peak inverse about 325 V). There they are silicon or SiC parts; Schottky types appear on the low-voltage output side of the charger.
fix: Rewrite as: 'In the low-voltage output stage of a charger, Schottky diodes cut the forward drop and the loss; the mains-side bridge uses silicon or silicon-carbide parts.'
